The owner's own GET /v1/conversations/:id/assets/:assetId answers 404 for a ready pipeline asset: that route reads the older transcript-reference store, so it is not a door to pipeline files for anyone (cross-scope refusal there is trivial). The model declined to run the ten-file catastrophic grep three times; the bounded behaviour over many files is measured by the component probe.

COMPONENT probe (dist/assets/files.js and matchers.js, in-memory repository and blobs, a pass-through moderator): not the product edge, not product UAT. It exists because the Chat tools have no direct door and the model declines hostile calls.

defects.title: Chat's ls/grep/read attachment tools are never declared to the model on a Product conversation
defects.expected: Spec (Attachments): retrieval is Unix style in both APIs: ls, grep and paged read. index.ts registers attachments.ls/grep/read 'for every Run'.
defects.actual: chatToolsForRun() (src/agentRuntime.ts) keeps a server tool only if its runtime name starts with `hatch.`, is Skill, or is in allowedExternalTools. For a Product conversation allowedExternalTools is corpusExternalTools(corpus), which holds only Creator http_function/mcp_tool ids, so `attachments.ls|grep|read` are filtered out. Asked to call ls, the real-Runtime model has no such tool; it can only reach the refused local file_* tools and tells the user it cannot read the file.

defects.title: Chat attachments cannot work on the real Runtime: every upload is refused because no content moderator is configured

defects.actual: POST /v1/conversations/:id/assets?name=report.md with a 300 KB markdown document returns 503 unavailable: "Uploads are unavailable: no content moderator is configured on this server.". src/chat/openChatAssets.ts constructs the AssetPipeline with options.moderator ?? new UnavailableModerator() and src/index.ts never passes a moderator, so Chat has no path to a ready asset. defects.title: A whole-document summary of a long attachment is built from about 1% of its text; the middle is skipped

defects.expected: Claiming a steered message and appending it to the transcript is one transaction that cannot deadlock with a steer (spec: the steer-or-start decision is atomic; no accepted message is lost).
defects.actual: 2 of 36 trials: the Run was failed with "deadlock detected" while 4 messages that had been accepted as steered (HTTP 200/202, journaled) were still unclaimed; they never reached the model. Likely cause by lock order: steerOrReplay locks the conversation row (FOR UPDATE) then updates the Run row; claimSteeredMessages locks the Run row (FOR UPDATE) then inserts a journal row, which takes a FOR KEY SHARE lock on the conversation row.
defects.repro: Scenario 5: send a first short message, then 3 messages (two HTTP, one WebSocket) at the moment its answer completes; about 1 trial in 36 deadlocks. Evidence ids: anomaly_trial_* in results/scenario-05.json.

defects.actual: Stalled Chat WS and SSE consumers stayed connected through every Run (4 trials, 0 closes) while 32 frames / 5883 SSE bytes piled up unread.
